definition: Professional Audience Safety System, the hardware used on projectors approved to scan audiences, used on selected units at Coachella 2025.
Pangolin's laser show control software, named in most festival case studies.
Software limits that keep beams out of set areas such as the audience, crew positions, balconies and glass.
Ending a beam on a surface so it goes no farther into the sky or the crowd.
The person responsible for laser safety at a show, usually the on-site operator.
A person watching the sky or beam path outdoors who can stop the beam at once.
The FAA's Notice of Proposed Outdoor Laser Operation(s), filed at least 30 days before an outdoor show.
The FAA's reply to an outdoor laser filing: no objection, or objection.
The FAA flight zone near runways where outdoor laser light must stay at or below 50 nW/cm2.
The standard an automated system must meet to replace human safety observers at an outdoor US show.
Sweeping beams deliberately through a crowd; in the US it needs FDA approval in the show's variance, and the Nordic regulators recommend against it.
The UK HSE leaflet on display lasers, which puts the duty on the organizer and points to PLASA's guidance.
A notice to airmen, part of the UK route for outdoor laser displays.
Lasers set up to throw beams into the sky as a landmark, as at Coachella's Quasar stage in 2025.
